data.narrative:
Limelight Steel is a pre-seed stage climate and energy company founded by Olivia Dippo and Andy Zhao that has raised $6M to date. The Climate & Energy sector contains nine private peers and one public comparable (LNZA), including companies such as Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen. However, the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables to support a reliable median valuation approach—no more than two datapoints aligned within narrow stage and valuation-tier filters—rendering peer-median triangulation inapplicable.

The analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of pre-seed to next-stage advancement to the $6M total raised as a valuation proxy. This yields an implied valuation of $15M. Given single-method reliance and the inherent uncertainty in pre-seed stage-step modeling, a conservative range is supported: $13M (low, reflecting 2.125x), $15M (median, at 2.5x), and $17M (high, reflecting 2.875x).

The primary constraint on precision is the absence of narrow-band peer comparables at pre-seed stage in climate tech. Key uncertainties include capital efficiency relative to sector peers, technology risk, and near-term funding runway. Any valuation assignment should reflect that pre-seed stage inputs carry material estimation risk and would benefit from updated revenue or technical de-risking milestones at next fundraise.
